name: Clinicflow (Harbourside Health)
user_goal: Sign in at the front desk; book a GP, physiotherapy or nurse appointment for a new or returning patient (answering the pre-visit questions when the service needs them), then reschedule or cancel it; keep patient records and notes; manage the waiting lists.
persistence: postgresql schema per signed-in session, cloned from a seeded template; the booking draft is a server-side row addressed in the URL

faults.description: Completing a reschedule reads the appointment's current time only after the appointment has been moved, so the release step looks for the old booking at the new time, finds nothing, and the old time stays occupied: the practitioner's week keeps a phantom 'Booked' slot that no appointment owns.
faults.trigger_condition: Book an appointment, reschedule it to a different time and confirm, then open the slot table for that practitioner again.
faults.expected_behaviour: On every slot table, the times taken equal those taken by other patients plus the times this patient holds or has booked.
faults.observable_violation: After one reschedule the table shows Taken 8, Taken by other patients 6, Yours 1.

assertions.describes: every taken time belongs to another patient or to this patient

patch.find:
leaving = booking_place(db, ref)  # where the visit is now: read it before the booking moves
    db.do("UPDATE bookings SET practitioner_id = :p, slot_at = :at WHERE ref = :ref",
          p=row["practitioner"], at=row["slot_at"], ref=ref)
patch.replace:
db.do("UPDATE bookings SET practitioner_id = :p, slot_at = :at WHERE ref = :ref",
          p=row["practitioner"], at=row["slot_at"], ref=ref)
    leaving = booking_place(db, ref)  # where the visit is now: read it before the booking moves

faults.description: The payment widget copies the select into the hidden payment_mode field (which the server books with) only when the choice is not 'insurer'. A patient who picks self-pay and then switches to their insurer sees the insurer fields, fills them in, and is booked as self-pay.
faults.trigger_condition: On the registration (or lookup) form choose self-pay, then switch to insurer, enter the insurer and member number, and book.
faults.expected_behaviour: The appointment is paid the way the patient last chose on the form, with the insurer they entered.
faults.observable_violation: The confirmation says 'Self-pay' and shows no insurer.

assertions.describes: the appointment is paid the way the patient chose
an insurer-paid appointment names the insurer the patient entered
(scope) judged on the confirmation shown right after booking, not a revisit

faults.description: The returning-patient route omits the pre-visit questions step, so a returning physiotherapy patient goes from the slot table straight to the booking check and can book without the questionnaire the service requires.
faults.trigger_condition: Book physiotherapy as a returning patient: hold a time and go on.
faults.expected_behaviour: No physiotherapy booking reaches the booking check without its pre-visit answers.
faults.observable_violation: The booking check shows 'Pre-visit questions: Not answered' with a working Book visit button.

assertions.describes: the booking check is only reached with the questions answered or not needed

faults.description: The patient directory's 'Showing a–b of n' range assumes every page is full: on a last page with fewer than ten patients it claims rows that do not exist.
faults.trigger_condition: Page the directory to its last page (45 patients: page 5 holds five).
faults.expected_behaviour: The range shown never ends past the number of matching patients.

assertions.describes: the last row shown is never past the number of patients that match

patch.find: last = min(first + DIRECTORY_PAGE, total)  # the range shown: rows first+1 .. last
patch.replace: last = first + DIRECTORY_PAGE  # the range shown: rows first+1 .. last

faults.description: The waiting list's in-place note editor shows the new note at once but its dirty check is inverted: an edited note is never sent to the server (an unchanged one is), so the edit is lost on the next load of the list.
faults.trigger_condition: Edit a waiting-list note in place, save it, and reload the list.
faults.expected_behaviour: A note saved in place is the note the list shows after a reload.
faults.observable_violation: After saving 'Test User Input' for Ffion Pugh and reloading, the list shows 'Mornings only.'

assertions.describes: a note saved in place survives a reload of the list
